## Tree Measurements 

### Tree Density Map
```{python}
#| echo: false
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning)

import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd

trees = pd.read_csv("data/processedTreeData.csv")

# Map center
center_lat = trees["Latitude"].mean()
center_lon = trees["Longitude"].mean()

fig = px.density_mapbox(
    trees,
    lat="Latitude",
    lon="Longitude",
    radius=10,
    center=dict(
        lat=trees["Latitude"].mean(),
        lon=trees["Longitude"].mean()
    ),
    zoom=13.5,
    mapbox_style="carto-positron"
)

fig.update_layout(
    coloraxis_colorbar=dict(
        title="Tree Count (Relative Density)"
    )
)

fig.show()

```
<br/>
**Figure 2**: Tree Density Map (Darker Areas Indicate Higher Number of Trees)

### Tree Height, DBH, and Average Spread Distribution
```{python}
#| echo: false
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

# Metrics to plot
metrics = [
    ("Tree Height", "Tree Height"),
    ("DBH", "DBH"),
    ("Average Spread", "Average Spread")
]

tree_types = ["Large mature tree", "Young tree", "Newly planted tree"]

# Custom color map by type of significant trees
type_colors = {
    "Newly planted tree": "#D7CCC8",   # soft beige/light brown
    "Young tree": "#81C784",           # medium green
    "Large mature tree": "#388E3C"     # forest green
}

# Create subplots
fig = make_subplots(
    rows=1,
    cols=3,
    subplot_titles=[m[0] for m in metrics]
)

# Add initial traces (first tree type)
initial_type = tree_types[0]

for col, (_, column_name) in enumerate(metrics, start=1):
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Histogram(
            x=trees.loc[
                trees["Type of Significant Trees"] == initial_type,
                column_name
            ],
            nbinsx=15,
            marker_color=type_colors[initial_type],
            showlegend=False
        ),
        row=1,
        col=col
    )

# Dropdown buttons
buttons = []

for ttype in tree_types:
    buttons.append(
        dict(
            label=ttype,
            method="update",
            args=[
                {
                    "x": [
                        trees.loc[
                            trees["Type of Significant Trees"] == ttype,
                            col_name
                        ]
                        for _, col_name in metrics
                    ],
                    "marker.color": [type_colors[ttype]] * len(metrics)
                }
            ]
        )
    )

# Layout updates
fig.update_layout(
    updatemenus=[
        dict(
            buttons=buttons,
            direction="down",
            showactive=True,
            x=0.5,
            y=1.2,          # moved higher
            xanchor="center",
            yanchor="top"
        )
    ],
    bargap=0.2,
    height=450
)

# Axis labels
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Value")
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Count")

fig

```
<br/>
**Figure 3**: Histogram of Tree Height, DBH, Average Spread for Each Type of Signficiant Trees. Toggle to switch between each type of trees. 

### Large Mature Trees Concentrate at Kells Park, While Newly Planted Trees Are Predominantly in JH-P
<br/>
```{python}
#| echo: false

counts_bar = (
    trees.groupby(["Site", "Type of Significant Trees"])
         .size()
         .reset_index(name="Count")
)

# Order sites by total number of trees (descending)
site_order = (
    counts_bar.groupby("Site")["Count"]
              .sum()
              .sort_values(ascending=False)
              .index
              .tolist()
)

# ORDERING of type of significant tree & site location
# Define the desired order for tree types
tree_order = ["Large mature tree", "Young tree", "Newly planted tree"]

# PREPARING the pie chart data
counts_pie = trees["Type of Significant Trees"].value_counts().reindex(tree_order, fill_value=0)
total_trees = counts_pie.sum()

# Creating the subplots
fig = make_subplots(
    rows=1,
    cols=2,
    column_widths=[0.4, 0.6],
    horizontal_spacing=0.18,  # Increased to prevent squishing
    specs=[[{"type": "domain"}, {"type": "bar"}]],
    subplot_titles=("A. Overall Type of Signficiant Trees", "B. Type of Signficiant Trees by Site")
)

# After creating the subplots
for ann in fig['layout']['annotations']:
    # Only adjust subplot titles (not main title)
    ann['y'] += 0.02  # move up

# Add pie chart with no legend
fig.add_trace(
    go.Pie(
        labels=counts_pie.index,
        values=counts_pie.values,
        hole=0.45,
        marker_colors=[type_colors[t] for t in counts_pie.index],
        textinfo="percent",
        texttemplate="%{percent:.2%}",   # <-- format with 2 decimals
        textposition="inside",
        hovertemplate="%{label}: %{value} trees (%{percent})<extra></extra>",
        showlegend=False
    ),
    row=1,
    col=1
)

# Add stacked bar chart
for tree_type in tree_order:  # ensures correct stack order
    df = counts_bar[counts_bar["Type of Significant Trees"] == tree_type]
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            x=df["Count"],
            y=df["Site"],
            name=tree_type,
            orientation="h",
            marker_color=type_colors[tree_type],
            text=df["Count"],
            textposition="inside",
            insidetextanchor="middle"
        ),
        row=1,
        col=2
    )


# Pie annotation
pie_domain = fig.data[0].domain  # first trace is the pie

x_center = sum(pie_domain.x) / 2
y_center = sum(pie_domain.y) / 2

fig.add_annotation(
    text=f"<b>{total_trees}</b><br>Trees",
    x=(x_center-0.03),
    y=y_center,
    xref="paper",
    yref="paper",
    showarrow=False,
    font_size=20
)



fig.update_layout(
    barmode="stack",
    xaxis_title="Count",
    yaxis_title="Site Location",
    yaxis=dict(
        categoryorder="array",
        categoryarray=site_order[::-1]  # <-- reverse the order here
    ),
    legend_traceorder="normal", # Proper legend order
    legend=dict(
        orientation="h",
        yanchor="top",
        y=-0.1,
        xanchor="right",
        x=1
    ),
    height=600
)

fig.show()


```
<br/>
**Figure 3**: Type of Signficiant Trees Overall and by Site Location 

Overall, the majority of the inventoried trees are large and mature (72.15%), as illustrated by Figure 3A. This indicates that the trail and parks are dominated by established mature trees rather than recent plantings.

As shown in Figure 3B, Kell Park contains the highest number of significant trees (30), followed closely by JH-W (29), while Lewis Park and Philips Park each have 21 significant trees. Together, park spaces account for nearly half of all inventoried trees (45.57%).

Figure 3B further shows that Kell Park has the greatest concentration of large mature trees (25), making it the site with the greatest number of high-value trees for ongoing monitoring and protection. Young trees were recorded only in Philips Park and JH-P, with JH-P also having the highest number of newly planted trees, highlighting these sites as priorities for establishment and long-term survivability.

### Kell Park Contains the Highest Number of Multi-Branch Trees
```{python}
#| echo: false
counts = (
    trees.groupby(["Site", "Multi-branch?"])
         .size()
         .reset_index(name="Count")
)

diverge_colors = {
    "No": "#388E3C",     # forest green
    "Yes": "#EF9A9A"
}
fig = px.bar(
    counts,
    x="Count",
    y="Site",
    color="Multi-branch?",
    color_discrete_map=diverge_colors, # <-- color mapping
    orientation="h",
    barmode="stack",
    category_orders={
        "Site": site_order                         # sets y-axis order
    }
)


# Put labels INSIDE every bar segment
fig.update_traces(
    texttemplate="%{x}",   # show the actual count
    textposition="inside",
    insidetextanchor="middle"
)


fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Count",
    yaxis_title="Site Location",
    legend_title="Multi-branch?",
    height=600
)

fig.show()
```
<br/>
**Figure 4**: Overall Number of Multi-branch Trees by Site

<br/>

| Site | Large mature tree | Young tree | Newly planted tree |
|------|-------------------|------------|--------------------|
| JH-W | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| JH-P | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| JH-A | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| PHIL | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| LEW  | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| KELL | 8 | 0 | 1 |

<br/>
**Table 1**: Count of multi-branch trees by site and significant tree type, excluding sites with no inventoried multi-branch trees.

Multi-branch trees provide greater canopy coverage, as multiple branches contribute to foliage and shade. Among the inventoried multi-branch trees, some may be codominant stems, where two or more large stems grow from the same point, forming a narrow “V”-shaped crotch. These stems can be structurally weaker as the tree matures and are most effectively managed through pruning while the trees are young (Mitchell, 2017).

As shown in Figure 4, Kell Park contains the highest number of multi-branch trees (9). Of these, eight are classified as large mature trees (Table 1), suggesting that this site would benefit from focused monitoring over time.

In addition, multi-branch young and newly planted trees were identified in JH-P, Philips Park, and Kell Park, where early pruning may help guide branch development and reduce future maintenance needs.
